citation: Westermann et al. (2023). The CryoGrid community model: a multi-physics toolbox for climate-driven simulations in the terrestrial cryosphere. Geoscientific Model Development 16, 2607. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-16-2607-2023
description: CryoGrid Community is a MATLAB model maintained by the CryoGrid research community for climate-driven processes in permafrost landscapes. Its public source implements a modular terrestrial-cryosphere model, with companion user-adjustable run files, setup guidance and a peer-reviewed description. Users supply meteorological forcing, soil and ground-ice parameters, an initial state and experiment duration. Outputs are simulated ground temperatures, thaw and related land-surface states for a site or configured spatial domain. Geographic coverage and temporal resolution follow those inputs. Both the source and run repositories state GPL-3.0 terms. A limitation is that model behaviour for a buried pipe, road embankment or foundation depends on local geotechnical calibration; a regional thaw pattern is not a structural failure prediction. CryoGrid can provide thaw and subsidence hazards for cold-region infrastructure simulation. The older CryoGrid3 repository explicitly directs users to this community version. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis is a separate possible forcing source. No MATLAB code, forcing or example archive was downloaded.
